artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, define
$$a_n \;=\; \frac{1}{10n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(154k+15)\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}(-2^{15})^{n-1-k}.$$

Here $\binom{3k}{k,k,k}=\frac{(3k)!}{(k!)^3}$. Let $E_0,E_1,E_2,\dots$ denote the Euler numbers defined by $\mathrm{sech}\,t=\sum_{m\ge 0}E_m t^m/m!$, and for an odd prime $p$ let $E_{p-3}(1)$ denote the Euler polynomial of degree $p-3$ evaluated at $1$. Let $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)$ denote the Jacobi/Legendre symbol.

Prove or disprove the following three assertions.

(i) For every integer $n>1$, the number $a_n$ is an integer; moreover, $(-1)^{n-1}a_n$ is a positive integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $5$, in which case $a_n\notin\mathbb Z$ but $5a_n$ is an integer not divisible by $5$.

(ii) For every odd prime $p$ and every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{154k+15}{(-2^{15})^{k}}\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}\;\equiv\;15\!\left(\frac{-2}{p^a}\right)+\left(\frac{-2}{p^{a-1}}\right)\frac{15}{16}\,p^{2}E_{p-3}(1)\pmod{p^{3}}.$$

(iii) For every odd prime $p$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{1}{(-2^{15})^k}\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}\;\equiv\;\begin{cases}\left(\dfrac{-2}{p}\right)(x^{2}-2p)\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }\left(\dfrac{p}{11}\right)=1\text{ and }4p=x^{2}+11y^{2}\text{ with }x,y\in\mathbb Z,\\[4pt]0\pmod{p^{2}}&\text{if }\left(\dfrac{p}{11}\right)=-1,\text{ i.e.\ }p\equiv 2,6,7,8,10\pmod{11}.\end{cases}$$
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this conjecture (concerning the integrality of the sequence $a_n$ and the supercongruences for $\sum (154k+15)\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k,k,k}/(-2^{15})^k$) was located. The conjecture appears in Z.-W. Sun's lists of open conjectures on congruences and is not marked as proved in publicly available updates known to us; status is therefore taken as unknown.
